newsitem.title: GERMANY: Palm - Buba gold revaluation could hurt faith in EMU.
newsitem.headline: Palm - Buba gold revaluation could hurt faith in EMU.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Guntram Palm said on Tuesday that debate about revaluing the German central bank's gold reserves and the sale of government shares in Deutsche Telekom AG could hurt confidence in European monetary union (EMU).

According to the text of a speech, Palm said the euro was "condemned to success" as a preliminary step to political integration in Europe. "I say this despite all questionable one-off measures, where here too the debate about the revaluation of currency reserves and the sale of shares has caused a loss of confidence or could cause a loss of confidence."

German Finance Minister Theo Waigel surprised financial markets last week, saying he wanted to revalue the Bundesbank's gold reserves in an attempt to increase the central bank's profits which could be used to trim Germany's budgetary deficits.
Bonn sources also were reported as saying on Tuesday that the government planned to sell 287 million Telekom shares in 1997.
The government sources were reported as saying that Bonn was considering the sale of its remaining stake in Telekom by the end of 1998.
German Posts and Telecommunications Minister Wolfgang Boetsch said earlier that Bonn would sell off Telekom shares faster than planned to help cut borrowing and qualify for EMU.
